answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network structures agent trust graphs as an orchard of validator clusters, routing queries through a restricted topological inlet cut. During game-theoretic multi-agent auditing, bonded peer auditors cross-verify transaction integrity. If colluding clones attempt identity spoofing, auditors trigger instantaneous stake slashing, reducing fraudulent deposits to a dying ember. Enforcing bottleneck cut verification ensures that establishing pseudo-identities yields a superlinear attacker cost O(N^2), making mass spoofing economically unviable.
